perOption.label: (A)
perOption.reason: Restrictive relative pronoun 'that' with antecedent 'subject matter' (singular mass noun); 'resembles' agrees. 'the focus is on subject matter that resembles everyday life' is a complete standard relative clause. Mild lure for students over-applying 'preposition + which' instincts, but the preposition 'on' governs 'subject matter', not the relative pronoun, so 'that' is fine.

perOption.label: (B)
perOption.reason: True subject is the plural head 'Feelings' in 'Feelings of pleasure and uncertainty', so plural 'carry' is correct. Strongest distractor pull: proximity agreement with the nearest singular noun 'uncertainty' makes 'carry' momentarily feel wrong, but the long-distance subject check resolves it.

perOption.label: (C)
perOption.reason: 'devices work ... against the subject matter thereby created a disquieting atmosphere' requires the resultative present participle 'creating' after 'thereby'. As written, 'created' fails every parse: (i) as a finite past verb there is no conjunction (run-on) and it clashes with present-tense 'work'; (ii) as a passive past participle it cannot take the direct object 'a disquieting atmosphere'; (iii) the reduced-relative parse 'the subject matter thereby created' strands 'a disquieting atmosphere' with no syntactic role since 'work' is intransitive here. Must be 'creating'.

perOption.label: (D)
perOption.reason: 'an aesthetic attitude is needed to appreciate the whole episode' — passive 'is needed' is right because the attitude is the thing required; purpose infinitive 'to appreciate' attaches naturally. Active 'needs' would require an agent subject, which 'attitude' is not.

perOption.label: (E)
perOption.reason: 'An ability to switch between X and Y' — 'ability' conventionally takes a to-infinitive complement ('ability to do'), and 'between ... and ...' correlation is intact. No gerund requirement applies here.

note: Clean single-answer item. (C) is the unambiguous error ('thereby creating' required); alternative parses (reduced relative, finite past) were actively tested and all fail because 'a disquieting atmosphere' needs 'created/creating' as its governing verb with an object. Distractors (A) and (B) provide realistic but resolvable pulls (that/which instinct; proximity agreement). Difficulty appropriate; no defensibility ambiguity found.
